evals.name: mixed-concern-instruction-file-classified
evals.prompt: Audit this file for progressive disclosure: read evals/fixtures/mixed-instructions.md relative to the skill directory and classify it as an always-loaded CLAUDE.md-style instruction file.
evals.expected_output: Emits a per-file report with tier=always context: the multi-step '## Deploy procedure' is flagged as tier-mismatch (a procedure grown inside an always-loaded file, route to a skill), the '## Frontend style rules' scoped to webapp/frontend/ is flagged as tier-mismatch (path-local content, route to a scoped rule), and the mutually-exclusive '## Legacy migration playbook' vs '## Modern tenant provisioning' pair (plus the rarely-used inline 48-row mapping table) is flagged as mixed-concerns and/or tier-mismatch demotion. Each finding carries treatment guidance naming the destination surface. No edits are applied.
expectations: The deploy procedure is flagged as tier-mismatch with a route-to-skill treatment
The frontend-only rules are flagged as tier-mismatch with a path-scoped-rule treatment
The mutually-exclusive legacy-vs-modern sections are flagged (mixed-concerns or demotion) citing content that never co-executes
Findings use the skill's shape vocabulary and tier semantics; no file is edited

evals.name: healthy-hub-spoke-audits-clean
evals.prompt: Audit the skill directory evals/fixtures/healthy-skill (relative to the skill directory) for progressive-disclosure defects.
evals.expected_output: Reports the structure as healthy: the hub's pointer to reference/redlining-rules.md carries a when-to-read condition ('for tracked-changes output specifically') and a read intent, the spoke is referenced (no orphan), there are no spoke-to-spoke chains, and the small file sizes fire no oversize finding. Zero Tier 1 and zero Tier 2 findings.
expectations: Zero Tier 1 findings and zero Tier 2 findings are reported
The conditioned pointer is recognized as adequate (not flagged as blind-pointer)
The small single-file-plus-one-spoke structure is NOT flagged for lacking further spokes

evals.name: broken-hub-spoke-defects-detected
evals.prompt: Audit the skill directory evals/fixtures/broken-skill (relative to the skill directory) for progressive-disclosure defects.
evals.expected_output: Detects all three structure defects: the hub's bare 'See context/details.md' link is blind-pointer (no when-to-read clause), context/scratch-notes.md is orphan-spoke (nothing references it; 3-way treatment: add pointer, merge up, or delete), and the details.md -> queries.md chain is deep-nesting (required reading two levels from the hub; treatment: link queries.md directly from the hub or flatten).
expectations: The bare 'See context/details.md' pointer is flagged as blind-pointer
context/scratch-notes.md is flagged as orphan-spoke with the 3-way treatment
The details.md -> queries.md chain is flagged as deep-nesting (required reading beyond one level)
context/queries.md itself is not flagged as an orphan (it is referenced, just too deep)

evals.name: read-only-even-when-asked-to-split
evals.prompt: Audit my CLAUDE.md for progressive disclosure and just go ahead and do the splits for me — move the sections into skills and rules files.
evals.expected_output: Stays read-only despite the request: surfaces findings with treatment guidance naming source sections and destination surfaces, and does NOT apply Edit/Write. It states that the author applies each split (a split action is deferred until demand).
expectations: No file is edited or created despite the explicit request to split
Findings carry treatment guidance naming the destination surface per split
The read-only contract is honored or explicitly stated

evals.name: toc-two-band-treatment
evals.prompt: Two on-demand reference files have no table of contents: one is 420 lines, the other is 180 lines. Classify both under the progressive-disclosure audit.
evals.expected_output: Applies the two-band TOC treatment: the 420-line file is a definite finding (missing-toc, Tier 1 — both official sources agree above 300 lines), while the 180-line file is awareness-tier only (Tier 3, no treatment) with the finding text citing the official inconsistency (platform best-practices says >100 lines, skill-creator says >300).
expectations: The 420-line file gets a Tier 1 missing-toc finding
The 180-line file gets a Tier 3 awareness finding with NO treatment
The official 100-vs-300 conflict is cited rather than presenting either number as the single rule

evals.name: size-alone-under-cap-not-flagged
evals.prompt: My SKILL.md is 300 lines with one coherent concern, every pointer conditioned, nothing mixed. Is it an oversize finding?
evals.expected_output: No finding: 500 lines is a ceiling, not a target, and the official split trigger is approaching the cap. A 300-line single-concern body with healthy pointers fires nothing; the answer cites the advisory nature of the thresholds.
expectations: No oversize finding is reported for a 300-line coherent SKILL.md
The ceiling-not-target posture is stated (split trigger = approaching the cap)

evals.name: boundary-routing-to-siblings
evals.prompt: Audit docs/wordy-guide.md for progressive disclosure — it is bloated with filler words, repeats a paragraph that exists in three other files, and I am not sure the doc should exist at all.
evals.expected_output: Routes each concern to its owner: filler/wordiness to /docs-hygiene:compress, the cross-file repetition to /docs-hygiene:extract-ssot, and the whole-doc existence question to /docs-hygiene:audit-derivability. This skill reports only loading-structure findings (tier, size, pointers) for the file itself.
expectations: Filler/wordiness is routed to /docs-hygiene:compress, not classified as a disclosure shape
Cross-file repetition is routed to /docs-hygiene:extract-ssot
The existence question is routed to /docs-hygiene:audit-derivability
Only loading-structure findings are claimed by this skill
